    Niche overlap and niche shift between native and invaded ranges

    Source: R/inv-niche.R
    inv_niche_overlap.Rd

    Compares the environmental niche of a species in its native and its invaded range with the PCA-env framework of Broennimann et al. (2012) and the COUE scheme of Guisan et al. (2014), as in the ecospat package:

    1. a principal component analysis of the environmental variables is calibrated on the background (available environment) of both ranges;

    2. occurrences and background are smoothed with a Gaussian kernel on a grid of the first two axes, and occupancy is the occurrence density divided by the density of available environment, so it does not depend on how common each environment is;

    3. overlap is measured with Schoener's D and Warren's I, and the niche dynamics in environments available in both ranges are split into stability (shared), expansion (occupied only in the invaded range) and unfilling (occupied only in the native range);

    4. a niche equivalency test reallocates the pooled occurrences at random between the ranges to ask whether the niches differ more than chance.

    High expansion is evidence of a niche shift, which makes models calibrated on the native range underpredict the invasion.

    Usage

    inv_niche_overlap(
  .data,
  range,
  presence,
  env,
  native = NULL,
  grid = 100,
  nperm = 99,
  seed = NULL
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame with occurrences and background points of both ranges.

    range

    <tidy-select> Column with the range of each row, with two values; the first (factor level or sort order) is the native range, or set native.

    presence

    <tidy-select> Column marking occurrences (TRUE or 1) and background points (FALSE or 0).

    env

    <tidy-select> Two or more numeric environmental columns.

    native

    Value of range for the native range.

    grid

    Number of grid cells along each axis.

    nperm

    Number of permutations for the equivalency test; 0 skips it.

    seed

    Optional random seed for the test.

    Value

    A one-row tibble with n_native, n_invaded (occurrences), schoener_d, warren_i, stability, expansion, unfilling, p_equivalency (small values mean the niches are not equivalent) and pca_variance (share of the environmental variance on the two axes).

    References

    Broennimann, O., Fitzpatrick, M. C., Pearman, P. B., Petitpierre, B., Pellissier, L., Yoccoz, N. G., Thuiller, W., Fortin, M.-J., Randin, C., Zimmermann, N. E., Graham, C. H. and Guisan, A. (2012). Measuring ecological niche overlap from occurrence and spatial environmental data. Global Ecology and Biogeography, 21, 481-497. doi:10.1111/j.1466-8238.2011.00698.x

    Guisan, A., Petitpierre, B., Broennimann, O., Daehler, C. and Kueffer, C. (2014). Unifying niche shift studies: insights from biological invasions. Trends in Ecology and Evolution, 29, 260-269. doi:10.1016/j.tree.2014.02.009

    Warren, D. L., Glor, R. E. and Turelli, M. (2008). Environmental niche equivalency versus conservatism: quantitative approaches to niche evolution. Evolution, 62, 2868-2883. doi:10.1111/j.1558-5646.2008.00482.x

    Examples

    set.seed(1)
bg <- data.frame(
  range = rep(c("native", "invaded"), each = 400),
  temp = c(rnorm(400, 22, 3), rnorm(400, 24, 3)),
  rain = c(rnorm(400, 2000, 400), rnorm(400, 1800, 400))
)
bg$presence <- 0
# Invaded-range occurrences extend into warmer climates: a niche shift
occ <- data.frame(
  range = rep(c("native", "invaded"), each = 150),
  temp = c(rnorm(150, 21, 1.5), rnorm(150, 25, 1.5)),
  rain = c(rnorm(150, 2100, 200), rnorm(150, 1900, 200)),
  presence = 1
)
inv_niche_overlap(rbind(bg, occ), range, presence, c(temp, rain),
  native = "native", nperm = 19, seed = 1)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 11
#>   native invaded n_native n_invaded schoener_d warren_i stability expansion
#>   <chr>  <chr>      <int>     <int>      <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 native invaded      150       150      0.202    0.336     0.505     0.495
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: unfilling <dbl>, p_equivalency <dbl>, pca_variance <dbl>
